mexico/cdmx-zocalo.name: Zocalo, Templo Mayor and Historic Centre
mexico/cdmx-zocalo.description: The giant main square, an Aztec temple excavation and baroque cathedrals.
mexico/cdmx-zocalo.details: The Zocalo is one of the largest city squares in the world, flanked by the Metropolitan Cathedral and National Palace with Diego Rivera murals. The Templo Mayor ruins sit beside it. Allow half a day, and note that the palace is free but needs ID.

mexico/anthropology-museum.name: National Museum of Anthropology
mexico/anthropology-museum.description: One of the world great museums, holding the Aztec Sun Stone and Maya treasures.
mexico/anthropology-museum.details: The museum in Chapultepec Park has halls on every major pre-Hispanic culture, with the Aztec Sun Stone as the centrepiece. Plan three hours and start early. It is closed on Mondays.

image.title: File:Aztec (Mexica) Gallery, National Museum of Anthropology, Mexico City (9778512611).jpg
image.author: Gary Todd from Xinzheng, China

mexico/frida-coyoacan.name: Coyoacan and the Frida Kahlo Museum
mexico/frida-coyoacan.description: A leafy village district with the artist Blue House and a lively market.
mexico/frida-coyoacan.details: Coyoacan has cobbled streets and plazas, the Mercado de Coyoacan for tostadas, and the Casa Azul, where Frida Kahlo lived. Tickets for the Frida Kahlo Museum must be booked in advance. Xochimilco canals are nearby.

image.title: File:La Casa Azul (The Blue House), better known as the Frida Kahlo Museum, located in the Coyoacán neighborhood of Mexico City.jpg
image.author: Rebeccananonof

mexico/teotihuacan.name: Teotihuacan pyramids
mexico/teotihuacan.description: The city of the gods, with the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon, an hour from the capital.
mexico/teotihuacan.details: Teotihuacan is a vast Mesoamerican city with the Avenue of the Dead and two great pyramids, one of which can be climbed. Go early to avoid the heat and crowds. Hot air balloon flights at dawn are an option.

image.title: File:Teotihuacan Citadel View of Pyramids of Sun & Moon (9783332506).jpg
image.author: Gary Todd from Xinzheng, China

mexico/guanajuato.name: Guanajuato colourful hill town
mexico/guanajuato.description: A UNESCO silver town of underground tunnels, painted houses and the Alley of the Kiss.
mexico/guanajuato.details: Guanajuato spreads over steep hills with brightly painted houses, plazas and the Callejon del Beso. Tunnels carry traffic under the city. The funicular rises to a viewpoint with the Pipila statue, and mariachi bands play in the evenings.

mexico/oaxaca-city.name: Oaxaca city, markets and mezcal
mexico/oaxaca-city.description: A colonial city of food markets, craft villages and mezcal tastings.
mexico/oaxaca-city.details: Oaxaca has the Santo Domingo church, the Benito Juarez market for chocolate and tlayudas and mezcal bars. Cooking classes teach the seven moles. Evening zocalo life is lively. Day trips visit craft villages such as Teotitlan del Valle.

mexico/monte-alban-hierve.name: Monte Alban and Hierve el Agua
mexico/monte-alban-hierve.description: A Zapotec mountaintop city and petrified waterfalls with swimming pools.
mexico/monte-alban-hierve.details: Monte Alban sits on a levelled hilltop above Oaxaca, with plazas and tombs and big views. Hierve el Agua has mineral formations that look like frozen waterfalls and natural infinity pools. Both fit in one day trip. Bring a swimsuit.

mexico/merida.name: Merida colonial centre
mexico/merida.description: A white city of mansions, markets and Mayan cuisine in the Yucatan.
mexico/merida.details: Merida has the Paseo de Montejo boulevard, a Sunday street fair and restaurants serving cochinita pibil. Evenings have free dance and music in the plazas. It is hot, so explore in the early morning and the evening.

mexico/chichen-itza.name: Chichen Itza and a cenote swim
mexico/chichen-itza.description: The Maya pyramid of Kukulkan, with a cenote swim nearby.
mexico/chichen-itza.details: Chichen Itza has El Castillo, the ball court and the Temple of the Warriors. Go at opening to beat the heat and crowds, and combine with a swim in a cenote near Valladolid. Climbing the pyramid is not permitted.

image.title: File:Chichen Itza from the Air 1932 - Caracol and Monjas.jpg
image.author: Sigvald Linné

mexico/valladolid-cenote.name: Valladolid and Cenote Zaci
mexico/valladolid-cenote.description: A colonial town with a central cenote in the middle of the Yucatan.
mexico/valladolid-cenote.details: Valladolid has a convent, a plaza and the Cenote Zaci in a town park. Cenotes nearby, such as Suytun and Ik Kil, are a great way to cool off. Rent a bike or take a colectivo.

mexico/tulum-ruins.name: Tulum ruins and beach
mexico/tulum-ruins.description: A clifftop Maya port overlooking the Caribbean, with a beach below.
mexico/tulum-ruins.details: The ruins of Tulum stand on a cliff above the turquoise sea, with a small beach for swimming. Go early before the tour buses. The town and beach strip have cafes, cenotes and the Sian Ka an reserve. Sargassum seaweed can affect the beach in summer.
